l: Good, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: cannot_be_overthrown_by Evil [when opposed to Evil] Good is represented by the immortals and their powers, which cannot be overthrown when they oppose Evil. The forces of Good defeat the Awgwas and their allies in the battle.

l: Evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: can_accomplish terrible deeds [when unopposed] Evil is represented by the Awgwas and the creatures they summon, whose actions are devoted to harm and misery. Evil is defeated when the immortals oppose it in battle.

l: Flossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Flossie is an intelligent, swift, strong reindeer of the Forest, guarded by Knooks and Will Knook and protected by the Fairy Queen while away. Timid toward men outside the Forest, she nevertheless joins Glossie to draw Claus’s sledge. She secures permission for the first journey, wears Claus’s bells, pulls through the night, urges haste at dawn, and on Christmas Eve narrowly avoids punishment after returning late before racing home before dawn.

l: Glossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Glossie is an intelligent, swift, strong reindeer of the Forest, guarded by Will Knook and the Knooks and protected by the Fairy Queen when away. Timid toward men outside the Forest, Glossie nevertheless joins Flossie to draw Claus’s sledge. Wearing Claus’s bells, Glossie helps the first journey by leaping roofs and racing home, then enjoys Christmas Eve’s night journey and carries Claus swiftly back before daybreak.

l: Will Knook, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Will Knook, chief guardian of the deer, initially permits Flossie and Glossie to travel with Claus if they reach Burzee by daybreak. After they return late, he denounces their disobedience, seeks punishment, and objects to the deer drawing Claus’s sledge, but obeys the Prince’s order.

l: reindeer, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The reindeer are deer permitted to draw Claus's sledge on Christmas Eve, up to ten each year, if they return by daybreak. When assisting Claus, they eat casa plants; grawle gives fleetness, marbon long life, and the Pool of Nares gives sleek coats and beauty. Their fleet feet cross hard-frozen deep snow, pull Claus and his pack, leap rooftops, and race home before dawn.

l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Toys are Santa Claus's gifts for children, made and distributed as dolls, animal figures, drums, cymbals, whistles, and horns. As the number of children grows, Claus prepares larger yearly loads so no poor or rich child goes without a Christmas gift. He leaves the pretty, wonderful toys by sleeping children's bedsides, bringing happiness to children and their families, though parents wonder how he enters homes. After the Awgwas steal and hide them in a mountain cave, the Fairies recover them in time for Claus to load his sledge and deliver them.

l: sledge, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Sledge is a rude vehicle Claus constructs from wood-pile material, with two upward-curving runners, a short-board platform, and a stool. Before its first Christmas Eve journey, its harness is repaired and strengthened. Drawn by Flossie and Glossie, it carries Claus and toys swiftly over snow and rooftops south to children.

l: harness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: attaches reindeer [by collars around their necks] Claus makes a harness by twisting strong cords into collars for the deer and attaching other cords to the front of the sledge. He also uses cords fastened to the deer's antlers as reins, and later cuts the harness away so the deer can return to the Forest.

l: pack of toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: contains toys [of many kinds] Claus fills a pack with his prettiest toys and carries it on the sledge during the first journey with the reindeer. He empties the pack while visiting houses in a village and a large city.

l: chimneys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Chimneys are entrances that provide access to children in locked houses. Traditional chimneys have fireplaces and let Claus climb down to leave toys for sleeping children, then climb back up to his sledge. New-fashioned chimneys are narrow, may end in cellars, serve stoves, nearly trap Santa Claus, and are abandoned.

l: the first journey with the reindeer, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The First Journey with the Reindeer follows Claus, Flossie, and Glossie traveling by sledge through the night to a village and city, distributing toys through chimneys, then returning to the Laughing Valley before daybreak.

l: parents (of the children), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Parents are Santa Claus’s deputies: at first, some build houses that prevent Santa Claus from entering through fireplaces and cannot understand how he entered. Later they anxiously prepare Christmas trees or hang stockings for his visit; loving parents fill them after he leaves.

l: good deeds, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: bring fame Claus's generous work brings him fame that spreads into far lands, despite sneers from a few selfish people. His good deeds cause people to honor him as a Saint in their hearts.

l: Christmas Eve, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Christmas Eve is the annual night of Claus's journey. It is the time when he may use up to ten deer to draw his sledge and travels with toys or gifts to sleeping children, farmhouses, a village, and children around the world before daybreak. On his first journey, he leaves toys; on this night, stockings are first hung by chimneys and filled during his hurried visit. In later years, children hang stockings expecting him, while four little folk help complete the yearly work.

l: Claus's first Christmas Eve journey, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: delivers toys [to sleeping children] Claus's first Christmas Eve journey begins after the Fairies recover the stolen toys. He travels with Glossie and Flossie, distributes gifts at farmhouses and in a village, empties his sack, and returns before daybreak.

l: recovery of the stolen toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_completed_by Fairies [just in time for Christmas Eve] The recovery of the stolen toys occurs when the Fairies search through the mountain in a joined line and find the cave where the Awgwas hid them. They break open the cave and carry the toys to Claus shortly before Christmas Eve.

l: reindeer (Claus's reindeer), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's reindeer are a team of ten loyal, beautiful deer serving Santa Claus: Glossie, Flossie, Racer, Pacer, Reckless, Speckless, Fearless, Peerless, Ready, and Steady. Selected for likeness to lead deer Glossie and Flossie, they are strengthened, made fleet, and given long lives by plants. Wearing new leather harnesses, they pull Santa Claus's large sledge swiftly over land and water on yearly night trips around the world. Beginning with Glossie and Flossie wearing bells in the lead, the Gnome King gives each remaining reindeer a bell string over eight years, until all ten make merry music.

l: Santa Claus's new sledge, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Santa Claus's new sledge is a large, strong vehicle for swift travel and carrying toys on his yearly ride. Larger and better suited than his old sledge, it has curled steel runners with wheels inside, a high rounded dashboard and sides, and space for three sacks plus sledge-box toys. Though initially too heavy for two deer, it is pulled by ten reindeer over land and water.

l: the first stockings tradition, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The first stockings tradition begins when Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara hang wet stockings by the chimney to dry. Santa Claus fills them with toys. The children tell others, who adopt the custom; it helps Santa Claus find children and deliver presents more quickly.

l: Santa Claus's Christmas-night journey, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Santa Claus's Christmas-night journey swiftly carries him by new sledge and ten reindeer from chimney to chimney across the world before daybreak; after finding stockings, he fills them to shorten delivery time rather than seeking each child.

l: stockings (children's stockings), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Children's stockings are hung in a row by the chimney to dry after snow play. Santa Claus sees them on Christmas Eve, fills them with toys during his Christmas-night journey, delighting Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara; other children then adopt them for present delivery.

l: three little children (beneath the tent), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Three little children live beneath a rude tent of skins on a broad treeless plain, neglected and unhappy. Claus plants and decorates a pine tree with candles, toys, and candies, giving them their first great pleasure. They dance and laugh, and their parents become more respectful and considerate.

l: pine tree (the tree Claus planted), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus carries a wind-broken pine top in his sledge, plants it before three little children’s tent, and decorates its branches with many candles and hung toys.

l: Christmas tree, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The first Christmas tree begins as a pine tree Claus plants for three little children, then is decorated with candles, toys, and candies. Pleased, Claus later carries and decorates trees for children in poor homes, with some fathers obtaining trees for him.

l: Spirit of Death, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Spirit of Death, a spirit, hovers near Santa Claus’s bedside but retreats disappointed after seeing the Mantle of Immortality, leaving forever.

l: Mantle of Immortality, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Mantle of Immortality is the world’s only mantle, a unique robe existing since the Beginning and kept in a crypt of gold and platinum between earth and sky. It grants immortality to its recipient. After every immortal votes, Santa Claus wins it through loving deeds toward little children; it is placed upon him, restores his vigor, sinks into his body, and permanently becomes part of him.

l: council of the immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The council of the immortals, rulers gathered in Burzee, is summoned by Ak to unanimously decide whether Santa Claus receives the Mantle of Immortality; all vote yes.

l: immortality, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Immortality is presented as a gift reserved for one who truly deserves it, and no mortal had previously claimed the Mantle. Santa Claus receives immortality because of his noble nature and lifelong service to children.

l: Kilter, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Kilter is a silent, swift man and one of Santa Claus’s four little helpers. Before Christmas he gathers children’s letters, passing through houses and walls, then joins Santa Claus’s journey to distribute toys.

l: Wisk, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Wisk is a tiny, mischievous, lovable fairy and one of Santa Claus’s four little helpers. He suggests entering houses through walls when chimneys cannot be used, then tickles the reindeer and has his ears tweaked by Santa Claus.

l: Santa Claus's yearly journeys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Santa Claus’s yearly Christmas Eve journey distributes gifts to children, expanding as they spread across Earth; reindeer pull his sledge over land and oceans, following the sun to encircle Earth in twenty-four hours.

l: the four little folk, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Deputies of Santa Claus are four little folk who begin riding in his sledge and entering houses through walls, helping distribute gifts faster and continuing to accompany him on his yearly ride.

l: deputies of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: assist Santa Claus [by preparing gifts for distribution] The deputies are the loving parents whom Santa Claus asks to help with his work. They prepare trees and stockings and may place the gifts in them after Santa Claus has departed.

l: stove, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_a heating appliance [that replaces fireplaces in houses] Stoves are newly invented and increasingly used in houses in place of fireplaces. Their presence explains why some chimneys do not provide Santa Claus with an entrance into the house.

l: house, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: contains stove [in the new-fashioned houses] The new houses have narrow chimneys and stoves rather than the fireplaces Santa Claus expects. Santa Claus and the four little folk eventually enter such houses through the walls.

l: toy-shops, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: supply toys [for children, including sick children and birthday gifts] Santa Claus sends great heaps of toys to toy-shops. They provide gifts for children who are missed by Santa Claus, become ill, or need presents for birthdays.
